answer_1.quote: We propose an end-to-end approach for a new task of automatically generating an implicit premise given an enthymeme. ... We use BART as the backbone sequence-to-sequence architecture and fine‑tune it on the ART dataset, optionally enhanced with discourse‑aware commonsense knowledge from PARA‑COMET.
answer_1.outputs: implicit premise (missing premise) generated for each enthymeme

answer_2.quote: We use BLEU, one of the most widely used automatic metrics for generation tasks to compute BLEU-1 and BLEU-2 scores between the system output and the human written gold implicit premise. We also report F1-Score of BERTScore, a metric for evaluating text generation using contextualized embeddings.

answer_4.quote: We hired crowdworkers on the Amazon Mechanical Turk platform. Given an enthymeme they were asked if the generated implicit premises were plausible or not... Plausibility judgement considers whether the generated premise was grammatical, relevant to the argument, coherent with our commonsense and completes the argument.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judged whether each generated implicit premise was plausible, assessing grammar, relevance to the argument, coherence with commonsense knowledge, and whether it completed the argument.
